title: Workspace files can hijack Python imports
red-team-reference: SEC-01 (HIGH): Workspace files hijack Python version checks
assessment: Confirmed. validate-design runs python3 -c from the /workspace bind mount, so the current directory can precede site-packages and a repository jsonschema.py or yaml.py can execute as builder.
mitigation: Change both Python import checks to python3 -I -c so current-directory, PYTHONPATH, and user-site imports cannot satisfy the check.
Add cd / before validation checks; future document validation must use explicit paths such as /workspace/docs.
Apply the isolated-python rule to every future Python validator command.
side-effects: Local project modules and user-site packages can no longer satisfy imports, which is intentional because these checks must test image-baked dependencies.
Future validation code must use explicit trusted image paths and explicit workspace paths.
No new privilege or network capability is introduced.

title: pip can execute a source distribution as root
red-team-reference: SEC-02 (CRITICAL): pip executes untrusted distribution as ROOT
assessment: Confirmed. --require-hashes authenticates an artifact but does not require a wheel; the current pip install runs before USER builder, and an accepted sdist can execute setup.py or a PEP 517 backend as UID 0.
mitigation: Move builder creation and identity checks before the pip block.
As builder, run pip download with --require-hashes --no-deps --only-binary=:all: into a builder-owned wheelhouse.
As root, install only from that local wheelhouse with --no-index --only-binary=:all: --require-hashes, then remove the wheelhouse and lock.
Regenerate or reject the lock if a target package has no compatible Python 3.11 Linux x86_64 wheel; retain --only-binary=:all: so future changes fail closed.
side-effects: A package without a compatible wheel causes a deliberate build failure and requires a reviewed lock refresh.
The extra wheelhouse layer uses temporary build space but is removed before the final image.
Runtime package code remains a separate concern and still requires the SEC-04 sandbox.

title: Build-time network allowlist is only documentation
red-team-reference: SEC-03 (HIGH): Build-time network allowlist is documentation only
assessment: Confirmed. Containerfile comments do not constrain DNS, redirects, proxy behavior, dependency code, or the network namespace used by apt, curl, pip, and npm.
mitigation: Use a dedicated default-deny CI build network and allow only reviewed package endpoints or an approved package proxy; block direct IP, IPv6, host-network, loopback, and RFC1918 bypasses.
Invoke Podman with the named restricted build network and reject host or unrestricted network modes in CI policy.
Prefer prefetching all artifacts through the allowlisted network and running the actual image build with podman build --network=none and local inputs.
side-effects: Repository redirects and CDN changes require an owned allowlist update.
Prefetching adds cache and build-context management.
A proxy must not become a broad bypass; preserve TLS verification and keep proxy trust material out of image layers.

title: npm --ignore-scripts does not sandbox runtime JavaScript
red-team-reference: SEC-04 (HIGH): npm --ignore-scripts doesn't sandbox runtime code
assessment: Confirmed. --ignore-scripts suppresses lifecycle hooks during npm ci, but markdownlint, markdown-link-check, and transitive JavaScript still execute when the validator invokes their version commands or a caller runs the CLIs.
mitigation: Retain npm ci --ignore-scripts, exact package-lock integrity, and root-owned /opt/node as install-time controls.
Require CI to run all validation commands as UID 1000 with --network=none, --read-only, --cap-drop=ALL, and --security-opt=no-new-privileges, using read-only source mounts and bounded tmpfs output.
Disallow socket, credential, host-namespace, privileged, and arbitrary-entrypoint mounts; use a separate restricted job for any intentional link checking.
side-effects: Read-only execution may require a temporary directory or explicit output mount.
Offline execution cannot perform a networked link check; that must be separately authorized.
Third-party code still runs, but only as an unprivileged process in a disposable capability-free container.

title: Runtime network isolation is not enforced
red-team-reference: SEC-05 (HIGH): Runtime network isolation not enforced
assessment: Confirmed. The CMD and comments recommend --network=none, but ordinary podman run uses the engine default and callers can override command or entrypoint; markdown-link-check is network-capable and can become an SSRF primitive.
mitigation: Make the CI merge gate use podman run --rm --network=none --read-only --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt=no-new-privileges --user=1000:1000 with a read-only /workspace mount and bounded tmpfs /tmp, invoking only validate-design.
Reject privileged mode, host networking, arbitrary entrypoints, secret mounts, and runtime socket mounts in centrally owned CI policy.
For intentional link checking, validate destinations and use a separate non-host network with an egress proxy that blocks loopback, link-local, RFC1918, metadata, and internal destinations.
side-effects: The normal validation path is offline and may need explicit temporary output storage.
Networked link checking requires a separate authorized job and policy.
A negative network test must use a controlled endpoint and add no credentials to the image.

title: apt package versions drift
assessment: Confirmed. apt-get update and unversioned installs resolve current repository state; a digest-pinned base does not pin the later Debian package index or package revisions. This is the known shared P1-001 issue.
mitigation: Use a reviewed Debian snapshot or internal apt snapshot proxy selected alongside the base-image digest while retaining Release signature verification.
Maintain an apt lock/manifest for ca-certificates, curl, git, xz-utils, and dependencies; install package=version and assert the result with dpkg-query.
Make CI fail when the snapshot identifier or installed manifest differs from the reviewed record, and refresh snapshot and base digest together.
side-effects: Snapshot maintenance can cause failures when packages or dependencies change.
Security fixes wait for the reviewed refresh, so the refresh cadence must be explicit.
Signature verification must remain enabled; an unrestricted mirror is not an acceptable mitigation.

title: Default validator checks presence, not document semantics
red-team-reference: SEC-07 (MEDIUM): Default validator is tool-presence only
assessment: The capability observation is accurate, but it is not an exploitable container-security defect in P1-002. Both the Containerfile and validate-design explicitly document MVP tool-presence scope and the P1-017 follow-up.
mitigation: Make no merge-blocking security change for P1-002; retain the fail-closed tool/version checks.
Track schema, ADR, capability-matrix, and evidence-manifest validation in P1-017, using isolated Python and explicit /workspace paths when implemented.
side-effects: Pulling semantic document validation into P1-002 expands scope and introduces parser/input attack surface without fixing a current container escape.
The P1-017 follow-up should receive its own threat model and tests.
